info.bio:
Several bands use the name The Roosters:
1. A Japanese rock group
2. A Polish pop-punk band
3. An Americana group from Minnesota
4. Another Americana group, this one from Texas
5. A grunge band from Missouri
6. A Celtic punk band from California
7. A hardcore band from New Jersey
8. A British blues band
9. A British punk band
10. A Danish southern rock band
11. A garage rock band from Los Angeles
12. A Finnish rock band

1. The Roosters (ザ・ルースターズ ) was a legendary Japanese rock band, active from 1978 to 1988.

scenes.name: Los rockers de garaje
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: En 1966 no tenían nombre (Billboard los llamaba «rockers»); hoy se les llama grupos de garaje. La respuesta creativa americana a la invasión británica: chicos blancos de suburbio que ensayaban en el garaje familiar y tocaban en gimnasios, iglesias y fiestas, con cortes de pelo de Brian Jones, actitud de Jagger, fuzz, rave-ups a lo Yardbirds, Them y Stones y, casi siempre, un órgano Farfisa o Vox con un regusto siniestro de película de terror de autocine. Recuperaban la línea del rock americano de 1963-1964 (Kingsmen, Trashmen) que los Beatles cortaron en seco: «Hanky Panky» de Tommy James, grabado en 1963, fue número 1 en julio de 1966. Ese septiembre las listas se llenaron de discos duros: «96 Tears» de ? and the Mysterians (mexicanoamericanos de Flint, con un órgano hipnótico de otro disco), «Dirty Water» de los Standells, «You’re Gonna Miss Me» de los 13th Floor Elevators y «Psychotic Reaction» de Count Five, calco del «I’m a Man» de los Yardbirds. Quejas dirigidas a las mujeres, pero también una nueva confianza; quejas pequeñas que empezaban a encontrar un objetivo, como en «One of These Days» de los Roosters.

mentions.author: Jon Savage
mentions.text: …or drugs, the parents or the system – the dilemmas were acute. One record in particular caught that moment of compression. Released in mid-1966, the Roosters’ ‘One of These Days’ was perfectly poised between glistening Byrds twelve-string jangle and surf kinetics, between high Hollies harmonies and punk-mystical lead vocals, between teen yearning and universal protest: ‘One of these days when I’m of age / And nobody can tell me what to do.’ The Roosters were a teenage group from Westchester, a neighbourhood hard by Los Angeles airport. They’d started out in surf groups, then had their heads turned…

mentions.author: Jon Savage
mentions.text: …the band recorded two tracks: ‘One of These Days’ and the moody ‘You Gotta Run’, both sides of a single that quickly disappeared on release. The Roosters’ journey can be seen in the few photos still extant: from pompadours, waistcoats and bum-freezer jackets to beards, corduroy trousers and long, long…

mentions.author: Jon Savage
mentions.text: …Los Bravos, ‘Black Is Black’, Decca Herman’s Hermits, ‘This Door Swings Both Ways’, Columbia Dionne Warwick, ‘Trains and Boats and Planes’, Scepter The Roosters, ‘One of These Days’, Progressive Sounds of America We the People, ‘Mirror of Your Mind’, Challenge The Tikis, ‘Bye Bye Bye’, Warner Bros. The Mamas…

podcast.title: Formation and Gigs
podcast.body: Tom McGuinness formed this blues band with Eric Clapton, who was an art school friend of McGuinness's girlfriend. They played a few gigs around London before both members were poached by Casey Jones and His Engineers. "He'd formed a blues band, The Roosters, with a guitarist who went to art school with his girlfriend, and they'd played a few gigs around London before the duo had been poached by the minor mercy beat band, Casey Jones and his engineers."
